abdomen.method:
I checked all three landmarks myself with read-only scripts in /Users/nuinuri/workspace/anatomy-worktrees/acupoint-key-filter/.cache/adjudicate/ (abd_profile.mjs, navel_pit.mjs, navel_pit_th.mjs, bone_nodes_y.mjs, abd_remap.mjs, sim_seed.mjs) and the mesh.mjs helper.

(1) Umbilicus, skin.glb. I cast front rays (+z to −z) on a 1 mm grid over x ±30 mm and y 0.96–1.02. I fitted a quadratic to the rim annulus (18–30 mm out) and measured how far the skin sits below that fit. The pit is about 8 mm deep. Its deepest point is [0, 0.990, z 0.1065]. The depth-weighted centroid is x −0.0008, y 0.9888 (pit >3 mm deep), 0.9888 (>4 mm) and 0.9890 (>5 mm). The core runs from y 0.981 to 0.994. At y 1.005 the midline skin is smooth (z 0.1129), so the old CV8 at y 1.005 is 1.6 cm above the navel. I use U = 0.989, the same as ST25.

(2) Symphysis, bone.glb. The highest point of the right hip bone FMA16586 near the midline is [−0.0061, 0.8266, 0.0412] (x > −0.008 to −0.01). The left hip bone FMA16587 gives 0.8263–0.8267 at x 0.0057–0.0061. The pubic crest stays at y 0.827 out to x −0.021, and the pubic tubercle rises to 0.829–0.834 at x −0.03 to −0.036. S = 0.8266. The old CV2 at 0.848 is 2.14 cm above it, which confirms the reviewers.

(3) Xiphisternal junction. The lowest point of the sternal body FMA7487 is 1.2006, but that is at its lateral corner (x −0.0109). At the anterior midline its lower border is 1.2025 (vertices [−0.003, 1.2025, 0.1077] and [0.0016, 1.2025, 0.1077]). The xiphoid process FMA7488 (y 1.1825–1.2046) has its anterior upper edge at 1.2024–1.2025 at x 0. The junction midpoint is therefore X = 1.2025 (range 1.2006–1.2046). The old CV16 at 1.214 is 1.15 cm above it (1.34 cm above the 1.2006 corner).

Scales, using heights in y in the frontal plane (the convention already used by the project): upper cun = (1.2025 − 0.989)/8 = 0.02669 m; lower cun = (0.989 − 0.8266)/5 = 0.03248 m.

For each point I kept x and the front surface, set y from its WHO cun offset, and set z to the first front-ray hit on the outer skin. I then simulated the new-seed path of scripts/build-anchors.mjs for both sides: front-face axis ray, nearest hit within 6/10/7.5 cm, and the outerSurface open-air test with 512 directions. Every right seed lands 0 mm from its skin hit and passes as 'open'. Every left mirror lands within 1.5 mm and passes as 'open'. None was lifted, enclosed or missing.

Full results with both sides are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-nuinuri-workspace-anatomy/e58f6abb-ce09-49a6-a5ae-3d125197a93b/scratchpad/position-review/abd_remap.json and abd_remap_final.json.

abdomen.risks:
1) The moves are large. Every remapped point goes down 1.1–3.9 cm except GB27 (+0.5 cm). The biggest changes are ST29 −3.9 cm, ST28 −3.2, LR12 −2.8, SP13 −2.8, SP14 −2.7, ST27 −2.7, KI11 −2.6 and ST30 −2.5. Each new seed differs from its old one, so build-anchors re-projects it by axis ray; ST25 keeps its anchor. After rebuilding, re-inspect skin, muscle and bone images, and update the authoring record and point-card text.

2) Horizontal positions are kept as the brief asks, but several do not match the WHO transverse cun. With ST17 x −0.09 = 4 cun, 1 cun is 2.25 cm.
- LR12 at x −0.043 (1.9 cun) is medial to ST30 at x −0.05. WHO puts it at 2.5 cun (about x −0.056), lateral to ST30. That is a left-right order error.
- SP13–SP16 sit at x −0.100/−0.108/−0.112/−0.130, i.e. 4.4–5.8 cun instead of 4 cun (x −0.09), and not on one vertical line.
- GB27 at x −0.131 is lateral to the ASIS (x −0.1145 to −0.119), but WHO says medial. GB28 (x −0.138) is lateral to GB27.

3) Neighbour order and overlap.
- SP12 (inguinal crease, unchanged at y 0.85, x −0.077) is now level with the new SP13 (0.8493, x −0.100, 2.3 cm away). The classical rule puts SP13 0.7 cun superolateral to SP12, so SP12 probably needs its own review. The older standard puts it at symphysis level, 0.8266.
- GB27 (0.8916) stays above GB28 (0.859).
- ST31 (0.808) stays below ST30.
- The thigh points defined from ST30 stay in order. Thigh cun is (0.8266 − femur medial epicondyle about 0.452)/18 = 2.08 cm. That puts LR11 (2 cun below ST30) at 0.785 against its current 0.792, and LR10 (3 cun) at 0.764 against 0.765, both in order. Before this change LR11 was 2.9 cun below ST30.

4) Landmark tolerance. The xiphisternal junction spans y 1.2006 (sternal corner) to 1.2046 (xiphoid top); I used the midline anterior interface, 1.2025. Using 1.2006 instead would move CV16 by 1.9 mm and the other upper points by at most n/8 × 1.9 mm. The bone meshes have only about 750 vertices, so landmark heights are good to about ±1 mm.

5) CV8 sits on the pit floor (seed z 0.1072, marker z ≈0.110). That is about 5 mm behind the rim (z ≈0.115). It is fully visible from the front but may be partly hidden in steep oblique or side views.

6) Heights are y differences in the frontal plane, the convention already in the record. The lower belly bulges forward (z 0.078 at the symphysis, 0.119 at y 0.96), so the distance along the skin between CV2 and CV5 is longer than the y spacing.

7) The two halves are not perfectly symmetric: mirrored left seeds land up to 1.5 mm off (ST27).

8) Earlier review texts that took the cun from 'sternal minY 1.2006 → CV8 1.005' (2.445 cm), for example GB25, LR13, SP21 and LU1, quote a navel level that is now stale. Their own landmark positions do not depend on it.

9) The female model has its own navel-based rules (data/female-acupoint-rules.json, verticalScale navel→xiphisternal/8 and →symphysis/5). Check whether any female anchors are transported from these male seeds; if so they need regenerating.
